brief: GS pushes its second rate hike back from October to December after August core PCE rose 0.25%, below expectations, with the year-over-year rate at 3.01%, also below expectations. Citing NY Fed's Williams saying there is no urgency, GS now sees a strong chance the FOMC concludes further hikes are unnecessary, even as Q2 GDP was revised up to +2.2% on stronger consumption. Pension-rebalancing selling of roughly $30bn, one of the largest on record, weighed on the market at the end of sessions but is now behind it. GS flags rising 10y/30y yields and midterm-election seasonality as the next headwinds, yet stays constructive on equities into year-end, noting the S&P is about 2% from highs and any rate relief would trigger a rally. Flows show mega-cap concentration: SPX has outperformed RTY for 7 weeks and XLK has outperformed SPX for 6, with MAGS seeing sustained inflows, RSP underperforming, and cybersecurity ETFs on pace for one of their best inflow months (+$950mm). On France, GS says Lecornu's targeted €54bn 2027 budget adjustment leaves the market understanding the problem at 120bp OAT/Bund spreads, but the bigger tail risk may be a weaker EUR if a future government confronts Brussels over France's EU contribution.
